### Inherited records in Node

Pass the parent as a nested object under its generated field name, such as `toBase`.
For the installed `GenericInheritance` fixture, the package's `grow` function takes:

```javascript
const grown = api.grow({ toBase: { base: 4n }, child: 7n });
// grown is { toBase: { base: 5n }, child: 14n }.
```

Here `api` is the imported package namespace. Its generated `NatChild` interface
names `toBase: NatBase` and `child: bigint`. Keep the parent object intact; a flattened
`{ base: 4n, child: 7n }` input rejects. Results contain independent copies and need
no disposal. Phantom type arguments add no runtime fields.

The [installed inheritance checks](evidence/inherited-records-20261008/receipt.json)
cover three direct exports over closed aliases with universe and phantom arguments.
Node performs 1005 checks and 1006 rejections; strict TypeScript checks the installed
declarations with `skipLibCheck: false`. Two builds reproduce the package archives;
installation runs offline after deleting the author sources and builds. These are
ordinary-source Node checks, not browser, React, worker, reviewed-inheritance or
configured function-specialization acceptance.

### Inherited records

A parent is a nested struct member, such as `to_base`, with its own generated type.
Use the installed header's layout, including when several Lean parents share fields.
The installed `GenericInheritance` fixture initializes a child like this:

```c
genericinheritance_nat_child child;
genericinheritance_nat_child_init(&child);
mpz_set_ui(child.to_base.base, 4);
mpz_set_ui(child.child, 7);
/* Pass &child to genericinheritance_grow with an initialized output. */
genericinheritance_nat_child_clear(&child);
```

The [installed inheritance checks](../evidence/inherited-records-20261008/receipt.json)
cover ordinary-source packages: 2010 C checks for plain single, multiple, multilevel
and overlapping parents, including a parent `Fin 10` field; 2011 C checks for
closed generic aliases with universe and phantom arguments. Both fixtures reproduce
archives from two builds and install offline after deleting author/build files.
Reviewed inheritance and configured function specializations over inherited records
remain unverified. See the [complete C consumer](../../tests/fixtures/generic-inheritance-consumers/c.c)
for calls, output cleanup and arbitrary-precision values.

### Inherited records

A parent is a nested value member, such as `to_base`, with its own generated struct
type. Construct that value explicitly. In the installed `GenericInheritance` fixture:

```cpp
namespace api = lean_bridge::genericinheritance;
const api::NatChild child{api::NatBase{4}, 7};
const api::NatChild grown = api::grow(child);
// grown.to_base.base == 5; grown.child == 14; child is unchanged.
```

Follow the installed header's field layout for overlapping parents; do not flatten
their fields or substitute C++ class inheritance. Returned values own their storage.
The [installed inheritance checks](../evidence/inherited-records-20261008/receipt.json)
cover ordinary-source packages: 2010 C++ checks for plain single, multiple, multilevel
and overlapping parents, including a parent `Fin 10` field; 2007 C++ checks for
closed generic aliases with universe and phantom arguments. Both fixtures reproduce
archives from two builds and install offline after deleting author/build files.
Reviewed inheritance and configured function specializations over inherited records
remain unverified. The [complete C++ consumer](../../tests/fixtures/generic-inheritance-consumers/cpp.cpp)
also exercises large integers and independently owned results.

The [installed inheritance evidence](../evidence/inherited-records-20261008/receipt.json)
covers ordinary-source C/C++ and Node packages with those nested parent fields.
The generic fixture checks three direct exports over six closed aliases, including
universe and phantom arguments. C performs 2011 checks, C++ 2007 and Node 1005 checks
plus 1006 rejections; the installed declarations also pass strict TypeScript.
Separate plain-inheritance C/C++ packages each pass 2010 checks for single, multiple,
multilevel and overlapping parents, including a parent `Fin 10` field. The packages
reproduce across two builds and install offline after author/build deletion.
These runs do not establish browser or reviewed inheritance, other native hosts,
or configured generic function specializations over inherited records.
